items.followUp: A pump lifts 50 kg of water through a height of 12 m in 8 s. Calculate its power in watts and horsepower. Take g = 10 m/s² and 1 hp = 746 W.

rubric.why: Identifies the given quantities and gravitational acceleration used in the calculation.
rubric.description: States the mass, height, time, and value of g in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the given quantities are correctly identified.

rubric.why: Uses gravitational work and the definition of power.
rubric.description: Writes the formulas for work done in lifting the water and for power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct formulas, or an equivalent combined formula.

rubric.why: Shows the substitution of the calculated work and given time into the power formula.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values into the power formula with units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution.

rubric.why: Obtains the pump’s power in SI units.
Converts the power from watts to horsepower using the given conversion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion and approximate answer.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 70 kg, h = 16 m, t = 10 s, g = 10 m/s².
Since 1 hp = 746 W, power in horsepower = 1,120 W/746 W = 1.5 hp (approximately).

items.followUp: Explain how a hydraulic lift uses Pascal’s principle to raise a car.

rubric.why: States the principle on which a hydraulic press works.
rubric.description: Explains that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct statement of Pascal’s principle.

rubric.why: Describes the main parts and arrangement of the press.
rubric.description: Identifies two pistons of different areas connected through an enclosed liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct arrangement.

rubric.why: Applies the pressure relation to the forces on the pistons.
rubric.description: Shows that the pressure at the two pistons is equal, using force divided by area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct pressure relation.

rubric.why: Explains how the press multiplies force to do useful work.
rubric.description: States that the larger piston produces a larger force that can lift or press a heavy load.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct force-multiplication effect.

modelAnswer: A hydraulic press works on Pascal’s principle: pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions.
It consists of two pistons of different cross-sectional areas connected by a pipe containing an enclosed liquid.
A force F1 on the smaller piston of area A1 produces pressure P = F1/A1 in the liquid.
The same pressure acts on the larger piston, so F2/A2 = F1/A1.
Because A2 > A1, F2 > F1; the larger force can lift or press a heavy load.

rubric.why: Identifies atomic physics as a field within physics.
rubric.description: States that atomic physics is a branch of physics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a branch of physics.

rubric.description: States that it deals with the structure and properties of atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the structure and properties of atoms.

modelAnswer: Atomic physics is the branch of physics that deals with the structure and properties of atoms.

items.followUp: A race lasts 18 seconds. Explain how you would use a stopwatch to measure its duration.

rubric.why: Starts measuring at the correct event.
rubric.description: Starts the stopwatch when the event begins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing when to start the stopwatch.

rubric.why: Stops the timing at the correct event and reads the measurement.
rubric.description: Stops the stopwatch when the event ends and reads the elapsed time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stopping at the end and reading the elapsed time.

modelAnswer: Press the start button as the event begins.
Press the stop button as the event ends, then read the elapsed time shown on the stopwatch.

items.followUp: Define random motion and give one example from everyday life or science.

rubric.why: Describes the defining feature of random motion.
rubric.description: States that random motion is irregular and has no fixed path or direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of random motion.
rubric.description: Gives an appropriate example, such as the random motion of gas molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid example.

modelAnswer: Random motion is motion in which an object moves irregularly without a fixed path or direction.
The random motion of gas molecules is an example.

items.followUp: What is inertia? Give one example showing its effect.

rubric.why: Identifies inertia as resistance to change.
rubric.description: States that inertia is resistance to a change in motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a body resists a change.

rubric.why: Specifies the state whose change a body resists.
rubric.description: Identifies rest or uniform motion as a state a body tends to maintain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to either the state of rest or uniform motion.

modelAnswer: Inertia is the tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of rest or uniform motion.
